exposure: Mode of birth (elective cesarean section vs. vaginal delivery)
outcome: Umbilical arterial (UmA) cytokine concentrations (IL-10, IL-6, IL-8)
Umbilical venous (UmV) cytokine concentrations (IL-10, IL-6, IL-8)
cohort: The study included 50 women with uncomplicated term pregnancies, divided into those not in labor who delivered by elective cesarean section (n=20) and those who delivered vaginally following uncomplicated labor (n=30).
finding: In uncomplicated term pregnancies, fetal circulating IL-10 is likely of placental origin, while IL-6/IL-8 are derived from the fetus, increase during parturition, and circulating levels are modulated by non-saturable placental clearance.
mod_finding: During labor, IL-10 concentrations increased 15-34%, and Group 2 (vaginal delivery after labor) showed increased UmA IL-6 and IL-8 concentrations compared to UmV, demonstrating significant placental clearance.
cross-section timing: At the time of parturition/delivery, before delivery of the placenta.
